title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign a 97.3% probability against a U.S. default by the end of 2027 primarily because Congress has raised or suspended the debt limit in every prior instance since the 1960s, preserving the Treasury’s ability to meet obligations. The statutory ceiling stands at $41.1 trillion following the 2025 reconciliation increase; debt subject to the limit is projected to reach that level around May 2027, after which extraordinary measures are expected to provide a six-to-nine-month buffer before any payment shortfall. Recent Treasury data showing debt near $40 trillion and affirmed credit ratings have not altered this pattern of legislative action. Factors that could still shift outcomes include an unusually prolonged standoff that exhausts measures earlier than expected or an exogenous shock requiring immediate additional borrowing authority without timely congressional agreement.
